plate.narration: A sheltered ledge looks out across the glacier. On an upturned sled, a broad map waits beside loose sheets and a warm lantern. Beyond the shelter, the ice stretches blue and quiet.

goal.text: Lay your pieces on Orin's map and find out what they show together.

steps.label: Lay your pieces on the map
Learn to hold an opening still

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, curious and a little spooky. Short sentences. Every choice shows its cost. Nobody dies.

npcVoices.Orin Vale: He/him, griffin scholar. Patient, plain speech, asks what a test really showed. Says 'whoever is moving the land' and never names anyone.
npcVoices.Lady Olivia: She/her, unicorn. Bright, certain, kind underneath; wants to use the openings to help people. Surprised by limits, never punished for disagreeing.
npcVoices.Bram Lock: He/him, bigfoot guard. Short practical requests, dry jokes, never orders the party. Protects Orin, mostly from his own ideas.
npcVoices.Seren Wisp: She/her, kitsune. Gentle teacher. Holds a condition, never changes where an opening goes.
npcVoices.Pip Thistledown: He/him, young manticore scout. Eager, quotes 'Lady Olivia says...', notebook and spoon. His choice mirrors the party's.

arrival.narration: The walking path climbs to a sheltered ledge above the glacier, where all of this began. Snow is falling out of a clear sky again. It lands, then slides uphill toward the deep ice, as if it wants to go home. On an upturned sled, Orin Vale has spread out his big map, the one with places that do not fit. "You found pieces that don't match it," he says. "Tonight we put them together and see what they show."

bram.narration: A bigfoot as tall as a door stomps past with a lantern on a pole. He is painting a line across the ledge with a sooty broom. "Bram Lock," he says. "I keep Master Orin safe. Mostly from his own ideas." Across the camp, Lady Olivia paces and hums. "She means to try something tonight," Bram rumbles. "When she does, I need everyone behind this line. Will you help me make it strong?"

choices.label: Go and see what Olivia is planning
Carry the stakes, bigfoot to bigfoot

check_line.narration: Bram hands out iron stakes as long as your arm. "Every stake goes in up to its hat," he says. The ice is as hard as a dinner plate, and the snow keeps sliding over your boots.
check_line.prompt: Hammer Bram's stakes deep into the hard ice

onSuccess.narration: Clang, clang, clang. Every stake goes in up to its hat. Bram ties a rope between them and twangs it. "That," he says, "is a line."

onFailure.narration: The third stake skids, and so do you, right onto your bottom. The stakes go in crooked, and the rope sags. "It's a line," says Bram kindly. "A wiggly one."

bigfoot_stakes.narration: Your bigfoot tucks every stake under one arm and pushes them into the ice with a thumb. Bram stares. Then he grins, very wide. "Finally," he says. "Somebody my size." He ties a rope between the stakes and twangs it. It hums like a harp string.

olivia_plan.narration: Olivia is drawing loops in the snow with the tip of her horn. "Orin wants to look. Bram wants to wait," she says. "I want to ask." She taps a loop. "Someone is pushing the land around. If I call one small opening right here, maybe it will tell me who. Imagine if we could use them, instead of chasing them!" Behind you, Bram is staking his line alone. It is coming out wiggly.

variants.text: "There you are!" she says first. "You helped me at the whale road. You know I'm not reckless."
"Oh. You chose the whales' way over mine," she says first, a little stiffly. Then she smiles anyway.

line_held.narration: Pip Thistledown, the young manticore scout, comes bouncing up with his notebook and his spoon. "Lady Olivia says tonight is the night!" he says. "Master Orin says tonight is for looking. I say tonight is for both!" He licks his pencil. Orin stands on one corner of his map to stop it blowing away. "Pieces first," he says.

variants.text: Bram's rope sags between crooked stakes, but it is a line.
"My whale-road friends!" Lady Olivia calls from across the camp, and waves her whole horn at you.
Lady Olivia gives you a polite nod from across the camp. She has not forgotten that you chose the whales' way.

tell_rivers.narration: Orin taps the great river on his map. "Start with the water," he says. "Only what you really saw."

variants.text: You tell him about the memory ice in the yetis' reading room. Deep inside it, long ago, the river ran out of the mountains by a different valley. Orin pencils it in: the river, leaving the other way.
Nobody here has stood in the yetis' reading room. Orin draws a neat question mark beside the mountains.

You tell him about the buried bridge on the mudflats, gray stone specked white like salt on bread. A bridge needs a river, and there is none under it now. Orin was there with you. He pencils in the river it must once have crossed.
Nobody here has walked the buried bridge. Orin draws a neat question mark on the coast.

tell_sky.narration: Pip is writing everything down very fast, with his tongue poking out. Then Orin points to the empty sky at the top of his map. "And up there?"

variants.text: You tell him about the island that came back early, and the mooring stone you copied there. It is carved with the land below, but in an older shape: the same mountains, with the rivers in other places. Orin copies it from your memory, line by line.
Nobody here has been up to the island that came back. Orin draws one more question mark.

check_trace.narration: Orin hands you a sheet of paper so thin you can see through it. "Trace every old line onto this, right over today's map," he says. "Slowly. The snow wants the paper too." A gust lifts one corner. Pip sits on it.
check_trace.prompt: Trace the old lines exactly, before the sliding snow smudges them

onSuccess.narration: Your lines come out clean and sure. Orin lifts the sheet to the lantern and hums.

onFailure.narration: A gust bumps your pencil, and one line wanders right off the paper. Orin rubs it out with his thumb, and you draw it again, slower. It is not neat, but it is honest.

fit.narration: Orin lays your tracing over his big map, and then he goes very still. The old lines do not match today's land. But they match each other. They join up, edge to edge, into one old map. "These places are not wandering," Orin says quietly. "They are being put back where they used to be. Someone is doing this on purpose." Even Pip stops writing. "Whoever is moving the land," says Orin, "wants it back the way it was."

variants.text: Look: the old river runs right under the buried bridge.
The old river leaves the mountains by the very valley the memory ice remembered.
And the island's carving lies over all of it, the same shape seen from the sky.

olivia_sees.narration: Lady Olivia leans over the map until her mane brushes it. Her eyes shine. "One old map," she breathes. "Then somebody knows how to move the land!" "Somebody who doesn't ask anyone first," says Orin. "Then somebody should ask them," says Olivia. Bram says nothing. He just moves his lantern a little closer to his line.

chime_pull.narration: The Listening Chime is leaning again, the way it leaned at the glacier camp and in every strange place since. But now it drags your whole pack across the snow, toward the deep ice where the snow is going. Like the goat kid that kept trying to walk home through the tear. Moved things try to go home.
chime_pull.prompt: Catch your pack before the chime drags it over the edge

onSuccess.narration: You grab the strap and hold on. The chime hums like a kettle and points one way only: down, into the old ice. Seren crouches beside you and listens. "It has never pulled this hard," she says.

onFailure.narration: The pack slides out of reach and bumps under Bram's rope. Bram stamps on the strap just in time. Your supper, inside it, is squashed flat. The chime hums and points one way only: down, into the old ice.

pip_runs.narration: "Down there!" cries Pip. "Lady Olivia says a real scout goes first!" Before anyone can grab his tail, he is off, sliding down the snow toward a dark gap in the ice where all the snow is pouring in. "Pip!" roars Bram. What will you do?

choices.label: Swoop down and scoop him up

check_chase.narration: The snow slides with you, faster and faster, like a sled with no sled. Pip is just ahead, skidding along on his tail.
check_chase.prompt: Slide down after Pip and catch him before the gap

onSuccess.narration: You grab Pip by his scarf right at the edge of the gap. Together you peer over.

onFailure.narration: You tumble right past Pip and land in a heap at the edge of the gap. Pip lands on you. Bram hauls you both back up by your collars, one in each hand.

check_call.narration: You cup your hands around your mouth. Pip is sliding fast, but one ear is turned back toward you.
check_call.prompt: Call Pip back up the slope before he reaches the gap

onSuccess.narration: "Pip! A real scout comes back to tell the others!" Pip skids to a stop, thinks hard, and climbs back up. "That's true," he puffs. "I'll tell you what I saw."

onFailure.narration: Pip does not hear, or does not want to. Bram stomps down after him and carries him back up under one arm, like a rolled-up rug. Pip is very embarrassed.

swoop.narration: Your griffin dives, scoops Pip up by his scarf and flaps back up the slope. Below you, the gap in the ice yawns dark, and the snow pours into it like sand in an hourglass. "Again!" says Pip.

passage.narration: Below the camp, a passage opens into the glacier, wide enough to walk down. All the sliding snow pours into it and is gone. Somewhere deep inside, the old ice groans. "The pull comes from down there," says Orin. "But not tonight. Tonight we eat, and we think." Pip writes DOWN THERE in his notebook and underlines it twice.

variants.text: From the edge you saw it up close: snow pouring down into the dark, and a faint shimmer, far, far below.

rest.narration: Orin opens the supper bag: dried apple rings and warm water. Pip pins a page down with an apple ring, then eats the paperweight. Lady Olivia sits apart, staring at the passage. Bram sits with his back to his line, like a wall with ears. Where will you sit?

variants.text: Your own supper is squashed flat, so Pip shares his emergency crackers. They taste a bit like map.

rest_olivia.narration: Olivia shifts over to make room. For a while she just watches the snow slide by. "At the Exchange, the snow fell on the fish stalls for days," she says. "People are losing their roads and their rivers. If I could learn to move the land, I could move it back for them." She looks at you. "Is that so wrong?"

rest_bram.narration: Bram makes room on his bench, which is a rock. Orin shares his last apple ring. "If anything goes wrong tonight, I have a signal," Bram says. "Two claps and a stomp. It means stop. Everybody stops. Even unicorns." He shows you, very softly, so he doesn't wake the glacier. Clap, clap, stomp.

olivia_asks.narration: Olivia stands up. "Someone is putting the land back on purpose," she says. "So it can be done! Let me call one small opening, right here, and ask it who." Orin frowns. "We don't know what an opening will do." Bram picks up his broom. Everyone looks at you. What do you tell her?

wait_seren.narration: Olivia sighs, but she waits. Seren takes out her ring of little chimes and tunes it, ting by ting. "If it gets big," Seren whispers to you, "I will try to hold its edge. Only its edge." Olivia taps her hoof. Tap, tap, tap. "Ready?" "Ready," says Seren.

go_ahead.narration: Olivia's whole face lights up. "Thank you," she says. "Finally, someone who wants to find out!" She squeezes your hand with her hoof, which is surprisingly hard. "Stand near me. If I'm right, you'll want to see this." Seren is still digging in her pack for her chimes.

summoning.narration: Olivia touches her horn to the empty air. An opening unfolds above the snow, as tall as a door. It shimmers with colors nobody chose, sliding and swapping like fish in a pond. Olivia stares. "No. Those aren't the ones I asked for." She waves her horn. The opening does not listen. It begins to pull.

pull.narration: Snow, papers and the supper bag go sliding toward the opening. So does the sled, with Orin's map flapping on top. Pip is running toward Olivia. What do you save first?

choices.label: Let the map go, and run to Olivia

grab_sled.narration: The sled bumps toward the opening, one hop at a time. The pull comes in breaths, like a big animal asleep. Grab the sled's rope while the pull breathes out.

interaction.cue: Grab the rope when the pull breathes out.

onSuccess.narration: You catch the rope and dig in your heels. The sled stops a whisker from the opening. Orin hugs his map.

onFailure.narration: You grab only snow. The sled tips, and one corner of Orin's map tears off and flies into the opening. Orin makes a small, sad sound.

onAssisted.narration: Bram grabs your belt, you grab the sled, and together you haul it back. Orin hugs his map.

run_to_olivia.narration: You let the sled go and run. Behind you it tips, and one corner of Orin's map tears off and flies into the opening. Orin makes a small, sad sound. But you reach Olivia's side at the same moment as Pip.

rope_holds.narration: The sled slides, bumps against Bram's rope and stops dead. Twang. The stakes hold like teeth. Orin's map flaps on its sled, safe. "Good stakes," Bram grunts, very pleased with everyone.

seren_holds.narration: Seren lifts her ring of chimes and rings one note, long and steady. The opening's edge stops growing. It still swaps its colors, and it still pulls, but it gets no bigger. The sled slows and stops. "Only its edge," Seren whispers. "Quickly now."

decision.narration: Olivia is still waving her horn, and the opening is still not listening. Pip has reached her side. "Help me stop her," says Bram, already moving. "Before it pulls somebody in." "No!" says Olivia. "Stand with me. I can learn it. I only need a moment." What will you do?

variants.text: A torn corner of Orin's map flutters at the edge of the opening.
She looks straight at you. "You know why I'm doing this."

choices.label: Remind her she only meant to ask

check_bram.narration: Bram plants himself between Olivia and the opening like a door. "Lady Olivia. Look at me, not at it." The pull tugs at her mane. You grab the end of Bram's rope so he can lean in.
check_bram.prompt: Hold Bram's rope tight while he walks Olivia back over the line

onSuccess.narration: You hold, Bram leans, and step by step Olivia comes back over the line. Her horn stops glowing.

onFailure.narration: Your boots slide, and Bram has to let go of Olivia to grab you instead. She stares at you both, then steps back over the line on her own, shaking. The rope has scraped your hands raw.

check_olivia.narration: Olivia keeps her horn up. "Catch the loose things," she says, "so I can watch it." Papers, mittens and Pip's hat go flying past you toward the opening.
check_olivia.prompt: Catch everything that flies at the opening, so Olivia can watch it

onSuccess.narration: You catch a mitten, a page and Pip's hat, one after another. Nothing else goes in.

onFailure.narration: You catch the hat, but Pip's notebook flaps right out of his paws and into the opening. Pip wails. "My notes! All my notes!"

orin_talks.narration: Orin steps up beside Olivia, quite calm. "At the buried bridge, the chime told us to wait," he says. "We learned more by waiting than we ever did by pushing. Let this one show us what it does, from behind the line." Olivia's horn dims. Slowly, she steps back with him.

signal_stop.narration: You clap twice and stomp, as hard as you can. Clap, clap, STOMP. Bram does it too. Then Orin. Then Pip, a bit late. Olivia blinks, and her horn stops glowing. "Everybody stops," she says faintly. "Even unicorns."

remind.narration: "You said you only wanted to ask it," you tell her. "It isn't answering." Olivia opens her mouth to argue. Then she looks at the opening, swapping its colors and pulling at everything, and closes it again. She lowers her horn.

beside_her.narration: You stay right where you are, beside her. Olivia takes a deep breath, and steadies. "All right," she says. "Let's watch it together. Nobody goes any closer."

stopped.narration: Without Olivia, the opening stops growing. It just hangs there, shimmering, doing whatever it likes.

variants.text: "You helped me at the whale road," Olivia says. "And now you've told me no." She takes a long breath. "I suppose friends do both."
Olivia looks at the rope, then at all of you. Her ears go flat. "You would all rather wait," she says. "I'm not very good at waiting."

stood.narration: Olivia watches the opening for a long, long moment. It flickers bigger and smaller. It swaps its colors. It pays no attention to her at all. At last she lowers her horn. "It didn't do one thing I asked," she says.

variants.text: "You stood with me at the whale road, and you stood with me tonight. That's twice." She laughs, a bit shakily. "Next time I'll ask it nicely."
She looks at you in surprise. "I didn't think you would stand with me," she says. "Thank you." Then she looks back at the opening, already thinking.

pip_choice.narration: Pip has been watching you the whole time.

variants.text: Pip stays behind the line, next to Bram. "Lady Olivia says a real scout goes first," Pip says slowly. "But you didn't go first. You stayed, and kept everyone safe." He crosses something out in his notebook and writes something new.
Pip stays right at Olivia's side, chin up, copying the way she stands. "Lady Olivia says a real scout goes first," Pip says. "And you stood with her. So I will too."

choices.label: Something drops out of the opening

fish.narration: Something drops out of the opening and lands on Bram's head with a wet slap. A fish! A silver fish, wriggling, a long way from any water. Bram does not move. "Someone," he says, "take this fish." The fish flips off his head and flops toward the opening, as if it knows the way home.
fish.prompt: Toss the fish back home through the opening

onSuccess.narration: You scoop it up and toss it. Plop! It sails through. For a blink you hear gulls, and smell a fish stall very far away. Then it's gone, home again. "Moved things go home," says Orin, "if you let them."

onFailure.narration: The fish slips out of your hands, smacks you on the nose and lands on Orin's map. Slap. Then it flips once more and slithers through the opening, home. Orin's map now smells very strongly of fish, and it always will.

lesson.narration: The opening still hangs over the snow, smaller now, swapping its colors. Seren walks up to it with her ring of chimes. "Nobody can tell an opening where to go," she says. "Not even Olivia. But you can hold what is already true: how big it is, how still. That's called Manipulate." She hands you the Listening Chime. "Hold it still while the opening is small, and it stays small."

choices.label: Show Pip how to hold it
Use your tracing to find its edge
Let our starweaver read its edge

check_hold.narration: You hold the chime out at the opening's edge. It wants to swing. It wants to hum. Seren whispers, "Don't push. Just keep."
check_hold.prompt: Keep the chime perfectly still at the opening's edge

onSuccess.narration: The chime goes quiet. The opening stops flickering and stays exactly as it is, like a held breath. Then, all by itself, it folds small and closes. Seren claps her paws.

onFailure.narration: The chime wobbles, and the opening hiccups one size bigger before Seren steadies it with you. "There," she says. "Holding is hard. That's part of the lesson too." The opening stays, small and stubborn, and Bram ropes it off for the watchers.

check_pip_hold.narration: You put the chime in Pip's paws and wrap your hands around his. "Don't grab," you tell him. "Just keep it." Pip's tail is twitching. Olivia is watching.
check_pip_hold.prompt: Talk Pip through holding the chime still without grabbing

onSuccess.narration: Pip holds his breath, and the chime holds still. The opening stays exactly as it is, then folds small and closes by itself. Pip stares at his paws. "I held it," he whispers. "I didn't grab. I held." He writes HOLD, DON'T GRAB on the back of his paw.

onFailure.narration: Pip grabs. The chime jerks, and the opening hiccups bigger before Seren steadies it. Pip goes pink to the ears. "Grabbing is a hard habit," says Seren gently. The opening stays, small and stubborn, and Bram ropes it off for the watchers.

hold_traced.narration: You hold your clean tracing up to the opening. Its edge lines up with your neatest line, so you know just where to hold the chime. It goes still, and the opening stays exactly as it is. Then it folds small and closes by itself. "Neat lines help," says Orin, very pleased.

hold_starweaver.narration: Your starweaver reads the light around the opening's edge and holds it with Seren, note for note. The opening goes still, then folds small and closes by itself. Seren's eyes shine. "You were made for this," she says.

lesson_done.narration: You have learned Manipulate. You can hold what is already true about an opening: open, small, still. You can never choose where it goes. Olivia has been listening the whole time. "That's what happened to me," she says quietly. "I asked it for one thing, and it did another."

joining.narration: Orin smooths his map and draws joining lines from one of your pieces to the next, until they make one old shape across the whole land. Then he draws a small arrow, pointing down into the glacier. "Wherever the pieces go," he says, "they go toward there."

variants.text: Something flutters down out of the empty air and lands at Orin's feet: the torn corner of his map, come back. Orin tapes it on, delighted.
Plop. Pip's notebook drops out of nowhere and lands in his lap. He hugs it. "It came back! It came home!"

ending.narration: Down the passage, the old ice groans again, and your chime leans toward it like a dog on a leash. So here is what your pieces show together: someone is putting the land back the way it was, long ago, on purpose. Who is it? And can you keep today's places where they are? Orin rolls up his map. "Tomorrow," he says, "we follow the pull."

variants.text: Olivia sits down beside Orin with her own notebook. "Show me how you test one thing at a time," she says. "I'm listening now."
Olivia packs her bag to come along. "It didn't obey me," she says. "But maybe I can help hold what's already there." Pip packs his bag right beside hers.
Olivia shoulders her bag. "I'll find my own way to the bottom of this," she says. She isn't angry. She is just very sure. Off she goes, and Pip stays with Bram.
Olivia shoulders her bag. "Orin wants to look. I want to try," she says. "I'll find my own way." She isn't angry. She is just very sure. Pip hesitates, then hurries after her, notebook first.
Behind you, the little opening still shimmers inside Bram's rope, marked for the watchers.
